title: unified-rollouts: improve observability and safety for canary/A-B/shadow auto-rollback
author: Priya Desai
description:
Context: as part of the unified rollouts effort we've seen intermittent production regressions when canary/A-B/shadow deployments trigger auto-rollback heuristics without good signal fidelity. This PR improves observability, metric matching, and adds safety guards so that rollbacks are both faster and less noisy.

High-level changes included in this PR: 
- Add rollout-level observability metrics (per-stage success/failure, matched-metric-name, windowed-error-rate) and tags for model_version, routing_policy, and customer_tier.
- Strengthen metric matching logic so that shadow traffic uses a more tolerant matching policy (prefix + fuzzy label mapping) while canary/A-B use strict metric match.
- Implement stabilization window and minimum sample thresholds before auto-rollback triggers; include exponential backoff for consecutive rollbacks.
- Improve canary sampling instrumentation to record latent KV-cache misses and sequence-length distributions that can explain latency regressions.
- Add e2e test that simulates a noisy metric source and validates that no rollback is triggered when sample_count < threshold.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics + tags implemented in runtime and exposed to Prometheus endpoint
- [x] Metric matcher tests + integration fixtures
- [x] E2E autorollback stability tests
- [x] Docs updated with rollout observability and safety guidance

Motivation: recent incidents (SUP-1284) showed auto-rollback flipping traffic during short noisy spikes, causing customer-facing flakiness. This change reduces false positives and gives on-call better debugging signal.

Notes on compatibility: default rollout behavior is unchanged unless a rollout opts in to the stricter observability guardset (configurable via rolloutPolicy.observabilityProfile). No breaking API changes.

Related: ENG-5043 for rollout lifecycle improvements, PR #318002 for earlier autorollback algorithm refactor.

Merge plan: squash-and-merge after final approvals; kept change scoped and gated behind feature flag rollout.observability_v2=true so we can stage adoption.
